version.changelog:
**Changelog for moltguard v6.0.1**

- Improved public documentation and transparency: new section addresses security scanner concerns, clarifies that the npm package contains full source code (not just docs), and provides verification steps.
- Explicit instructions to audit installed files, verify package size and contents, and review key TypeScript sources for privacy and networking logic.
- Clear explanation of all network calls, with code references for maximum auditability.
- Guarantee that only three local files are created/modified, with no external database or hidden operations.
- Reassured users of privacy: package uses local sanitization, open-source MIT license, and no third-party LLM calls.
- No changes to runtime/plugin code functionality; changelog is documentation- and transparency-focused.

llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (local prompt sanitization + injection detection) is plausible, but the published bundle contains only documentation that instructs the agent to install and use a separate npm package that will call a remote API — the registry metadata lacks the claimed source/homepage and the actual code is not bundled here, so you must trust an external package and remote service before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description (local sanitization + injection detection) align with the behavior described in SKILL.md (local HTTP proxy + an agent that posts sanitized content to api.moltguard.com). However the registry metadata shows 'Source: unknown' and 'Homepage: none' while SKILL.md repeatedly points to npmjs.com and github.com/openguardrails/moltguard — that discrepancy reduces confidence that the published skill bundle actually contains the claimed code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to install an external npm package via 'openclaw plugins install' and to audit code hosted on GitHub. The doc also documents runtime network calls: a one-time registration POST to https://api.moltguard.com/api/register and analysis POSTs to https://api.moltguard.com/api/check/tool-call using a bearer API key. Those network calls mean user data (albeit claimed to be 'sanitized') will leave the machine. Because no code is bundled in this skill, there is no local enforcement of the sanitization guarantees — you must inspect the external package to confirm what is actually sent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill itself is instruction-only (no install spec or code files), which is low local install risk. But it explicitly directs installation of a third-party npm package (@openguardrails/moltguard) via OpenClaw. That external install will write code to disk and run in the agent's runtime; the SKILL.md claims the package is auditable on npm/GitHub, but the registry metadata in this listing does not include that source link, so the user should verify the npm package contents before installing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, which is consistent with SKILL.md saying the plugin auto-registers and stores a generated API key in ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json. However, the plugin will create persistent credentials and send sanitized content to a remote API. That creates a proportionality question: storing an API key and allowing network calls is reasonable for a remote analysis service, but the brokered claims that PII/API keys are never sent rest on the unbundled external code — you must audit that code and the remote endpoint before trusting it.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forcibly always-enabled (always: false) and does not request other skills' configuration. The described persistence (storing a MoltGuard API key and JSONL logs under ~/.openclaw) is scoped to its own paths and is expected for a plugin that persists credentials and logs. Autonomous invocation is allowed (disable-model-invocation: false), which is normal; combined with network calls this increases blast radius but is not exceptional alone.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This bundle is documentation-only and points you to an external npm package and a remote API. Before installing: 1) Confirm the package on npm (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@openguardrails/moltguard) and that its contents match the GitHub repo the SKILL.md references; 2) Manually clone and audit the key files the doc calls out (gateway/*.ts, agent/runner.ts, memory/store.ts) to verify sanitization and network logic; 3) Confirm the api.moltguard.com endpoints and privacy policy, and consider whether sending even 'sanitized' prompt text to a third party is acceptable for your threat model; 4) Check the file paths and permissions (e.g., ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json) and be prepared to delete the plugin and its credentials if the audit finds unexpected behavior. If you cannot or will not audit the external package and endpoint, avoid installing.
